value.quartech_label: Are there soil test phosphorus and post-harvest nitrate results on record from within the last 3 years for the fields* where nutrient sources are applied?
value.quartech_textbelowquestion: *soil testing is not required in cranberry fields or in fields of peat or muck soils
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Sections 53, 54, and 55

value.quartech_label: If a field’s post-harvest soil nitrate level was 100 kg N/ha or greater, is another test conducted the following year to monitor nitrogen use?
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Section 53(1)(a)

value.quartech_label: Are crop yields for the fields where nutrient sources are applied kept on record for 5 years?
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Section 51(2)

value.quartech_label: Are nutrient application type, rates, times, and locations noted and kept on record for 5 years?
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Section 51(2)

value.quartech_label: Is the nutrient or soil conditioner application equipment operated to minimize soil compaction or erosion?
When liquid manure is being delivered to a field through pipes that pass within 10 m [30 ft] of any ditch or watercourse, is there secondary containment for the pipes?
Are potential sources of available nitrogen considered when selecting manure or fertilizer application rates?
Does the farm have an up to date (within the last 5 years) nutrient management plan if required according to the size, location and type of operation, and soil test levels of the farm?
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Section 56

value.quartech_label: Is the amount of available nitrogen applied from manures, fertilizers, and other sources determined and does the rate of application match the crop requirement?
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Sections 51(1)(d) and 52(1)(c)

value.quartech_label: Is application managed to ensure that nutrient sources (including drift from sprayed liquids) do not enter surface water, cross a property boundary, or have a direct path to groundwater?
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Sections 51(1)(b) and 51(1)(c)

value.quartech_label: Are nutrient sources (including manure and fertilizer) applied to avoid the following conditions: strong, divergent windy conditions*; storm events; water-saturated or flooded soils; and frozen or snow-covered soil?
value.quartech_textbelowquestion: *if nutrients are injected or applied below a crop canopy, they may be applied during windy conditions
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Sections 27 and 49

value.quartech_label: When applying liquid manure to tile-drained fields, are application practices adjusted so that manure will not directly flow into tile drains and discharge into a watercourse?
value.quartech_textbelowquestion: (use of practices such as pre-tillage within 7 days and/or injection and/or an application rate appropriate to soil conditions)
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Section 51 (1)(b)

value.quartech_label: Are nutrients* applied with minimum setback distances from sensitive water resources?
value.quartech_textbelowquestion:
• Drinking water sources: 30 m [100 ft] from a well or diversion point for drinking water, or 3 m [10 ft] 
if commercial fertilizer is used
• Watercourses other than diversion points for drinking water: 3 m [10 ft] or 1.5 m [5 ft] for commercial fertilizer 
or subsurface injection 
*does not apply to irrigation water that is a nutrient source
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Section 18

value.quartech_label: In High-Precipitation Areas*, is nutrient application avoided during November, December, and January?
value.quartech_textbelowquestion: *areas where precipitation is greater than 600 mm [24 in] from Oct 1st to April 30th, see Reference Guide Appendix B
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Sections 20 and 27

value.quartech_label: In High-Precipitation Areas, is a risk assessment completed and kept on record prior to the application of nutrient sources during the months of October, February, and March?
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Sections 20 and 27

value.quartech_label: In High-Precipitation Areas, are nutrient sources only applied to bare soil in the fall if a crop is planted before winter and the soil has a low risk* of leaching?
value.quartech_textbelowquestion: *generally, soils with medium to fine textures (silt or clay) are considered lower risk for leaching
value.quartech_textabovequestion: Environmental Management Act, Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management, Sections 20 and 27(3)

value.quartech_label: When using manures, or other nutrient sources (e.g., compost), have nutrient levels, (including C:N ratios) been tested to ensure that amendment is being applied appropriately (tested within the last 2 years)?
Are nutrients or soil conditioners applied only to cropland, avoiding sensitive areas (e.g., wildlife habitat)?
Is manure application and timing selected so that odours are reduced? (e.g., using injection methods and selecting time of day or day of week that minimizes emissions)
Are spreaders and other application equipment selected and operated in a manner to apply nutrients uniformly and in a controlled manner?
Has nutrient or soil conditioner application equipment been calibrated within the past year for rate and uniformity?
